canonical_name: Maschke complete-reducibility theorem for finite-group representations (exact formulation open)
literal_source_claim_zh: 有限群表示在特征不整除群阶时可完全约化
literal_source_claim_en: A finite-group representation is completely reducible when the characteristic does not divide the group order.
statement_blocker: The catalog supplies no source edition or theorem passage, scalar field, finite-dimensionality convention, representation definition, characteristic encoding, or definition of complete reducibility. Pinned mathlib has a direct complemented-subrepresentation theorem, while its future-work note says the usual finite-dimensional direct-sum-of-irreducibles form is not yet provided. Freezing either formulation at intake would invent or substitute missing mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: a source must fix the finite group and its order encoding, scalar field or division ring, carrier universes, representation convention, finite-dimensionality, and the semisimplicity or complete-reducibility convention.
conclusion: Prospective family only: a representation of a finite group over a source-defined scalar field is source-defined completely reducible when the field characteristic does not divide the group order. Whether this means invariant complements or a direct sum of irreducibles remains open.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before a proposition is selected; the statement phase must resolve the trivial group, zero representation space, characteristic zero, positive characteristic, finite versus infinite-dimensional spaces, and cardinality/coercion boundaries.
